record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: How do recurrence quotients behave for other families of infinite words, such as words of complexity 2n+1 or more general infinite words?

evidence.quote: Draw a study of the recurrence quotients for other families of infinite words than sturmian words, such as words of complexity 2n + 1, or infinite words in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u = u_0 u_1 u_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet $A$. For an integer $n \geq 1$, let $L_n(u)$ denote the set of factors (contiguous finite subwords) of $u$ of length $n$, and let $p_u(n) = |L_n(u)|$ be its factor complexity. The recurrence function $R_u(n)$ is defined as the smallest integer $N$ (or $+\infty$ if no such integer exists) such that every factor of $u$ of length $N$ contains every factor of $u$ of length $n$ as a subfactor; $u$ is called uniformly recurrent when $R_u(n) < \infty$ for all $n$. The recurrence quotient of $u$ is then defined as
$$\rho(u) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{R_u(n)}{n}.$$

For Sturmian words (binary infinite words with $p_u(n) = n+1$ for all $n \geq 1$), the recurrence quotient has been completely characterized: its infimum over all Sturmian words equals $2 + \varphi$, where $\varphi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2$, attained by the Fibonacci word, and its full spectrum of values is known.

Carry out an analogous study for broader families of uniformly recurrent infinite words. In particular:

(a) Determine the set of values, the infimum, and the extremal words for the recurrence quotient $\rho(u)$ as $u$ ranges over all infinite words of factor complexity $p_u(n) = 2n+1$ (for instance, Arnoux–Rauzy words on a three-letter alphabet).

(b) More generally, describe the behavior of $\rho(u)$ for arbitrary uniformly recurrent infinite words: identify natural classes for which $\rho(u)$ admits an explicit formula or sharp lower bounds, and characterize the words attaining the extremal values within each class.
artifact.status_search_result: Recurrence functions for Arnoux–Rauzy words (which have complexity 2n+1) were explicitly computed by Cassaigne, Chekhova and others, yielding partial results for the recurrence quotient in this family. However, a complete description of the spectrum of recurrence quotients for all words of complexity 2n+1, and for general uniformly recurrent infinite words, does not appear in the literature, indicating the broader program remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Fonctions de récurrence des suites d'Arnoux-Rauzy et réponse à une question de Morse et Hedlund
status_evidence.snippet: Cassaigne and Chekhova explicitly compute the recurrence function for Arnoux–Rauzy sequences and answer a question of Morse and Hedlund.
status_evidence.claim: Recurrence functions are known for Arnoux–Rauzy words (complexity 2n+1), giving partial results on recurrence quotients.

status_evidence.title: Recurrence in infinite words (Cassaigne)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing recurrence functions and quotients for various families of infinite words beyond Sturmian.
status_evidence.claim: The recurrence quotient has been studied for several families but a complete picture for general infinite words is not available.
